function: Learned beam selection for hybrid beamforming in cell-free joint transmission: CNN narrow-beam prediction prunes the action space, RL picks beams for delay satisfaction (pp. 4-6).
system: Cell-free massive MIMO, 3 BSs each with 8x4 UPA, 4 or 8 single-antenna users, hybrid beamforming, 28 GHz, 100 MHz, no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: CNN regression (supervised) for narrow-beam prediction; centralized D3QN, fully distributed D-DDQN, and QMIX multi-agent RL with centralized training for beam selection (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Own simulation: Saleh-Valenzuela UPA channel, AR(1) small-scale fading, 3GPP LoS/NLoS/blocked path states; CNN dataset 30,000 samples, split 21,000/4,500/4,500 (pp. 3, 10).
test_conditions: CNN: train/validation/test split of one simulated dataset (p. 10). RL: evaluated with 4 users, 8 users, and 6 BSs with 8 users (pp. 12-14); no cross-setting test.
baselines: Non-learned: LBS [19] (Lyapunov-based heuristic), HDLO (proposed); learned: MADDPG, SBA-D3QN (D3QN without wide-beam pruning, an ablation), D-DDQN and QMIX-PDBS (proposed) (pp. 10-13).
metrics: System delay satisfaction rate, per-user delay satisfaction rate, average queue length distribution, narrow-beam prediction accuracy, beam training overhead (pp. 10-13).
complexity: O(1), where O(1) denotes one ZF beamforming, versus O(|A_LBS|) for LBS (Tables III and V, pp. 12-13); no FLOPs, parameter counts, or runtime.
q1_support: p. 3: "According to the Saleh-Valenzuela model, the channel from user u to BS b at time slot t can be expressed as". Custom Saleh-Valenzuela simulator with AR(1) fading; 3GPP TR 38.901 [40] is cited only for the blocked/LoS/NLoS path states (p. 10); no CDL/TDL, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "The dataset comprises 30,000 samples in total, partitioned into three subsets for training, validation, and testing". Test data are a held-out part of the same data; the 4-user, 8-user and 6-BS results (pp. 12-14) are reported per scenario, and no test outside the training setting, fine-tuning or transfer is stated.
q3_support: p. 10: "a heuristic algorithm (LBS) is proposed in [19]"; p. 12: "in the MADDPG framework, each BS is equipped with an individual actor network". LBS (non-learned, 21.08% vs 70.71% for WBR-D3QN, Table III, p. 12) and MADDPG (50.87% vs 67.66% for QMIX-PDBS, Table V, p. 13) are compared on delay satisfaction rate.
q4_support: p. 11: "Table III presents a comparative analysis of beam training overhead, computational complexity and the system delay satisfaction rate". Table III (p. 12) lists computational complexity O(1) for WBR-D3QN, with O(1) denoting one ZF beamforming, versus O(|A_LBS|) for LBS; Table V (p. 13) lists O(1) for the distributed schemes.
q5_support: p. 10: "To construct the data set, each BS performs the wide beam probing followed by the narrow beam probing in a single time slot". The data come from the authors' own simulation; no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Included, area 3: the learned decisions are analog beam indices (CNN beam-space pruning plus RL selection) in cell-free hybrid beamforming. The reward is delay-based, but user scheduling is assumed done (footnote 1, p. 3), so the action is physical layer. No RIS. q1 is 0 because the channel is Saleh-Valenzuela and 3GPP [40] is used only for blocked/LoS/NLoS path states (p. 10); reviewer may confirm. q3 counts LBS [19] and MADDPG; SBA-D3QN is an ablation-like variant and is not counted. q4 rests on the coarse O(1) entries of Tables III and V; no FLOPs, parameters, or runtime.
